A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, Risk-Sensitive Agent Compositions. All 19 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original BucketedVaR evaluations on DroneNav, 16-Rooms, Fetch, and BoxRelay, plus correlated-Gaussian simulations. Outcomes appear in Section 4, Figures 2–4, and appendix Tables 1–2.

after.justification: V4 retains the original benchmark evaluations and synthetic correlation experiments, including numerical VaR/CVaR comparisons in Figures 2–4 and appendix Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The RMAG objective, BucketedVaR pseudocode, risk-budget allocation procedure, and CVaR approximation are unchanged. Bandit optimization remains a future direction.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same DroneNav, 16-Rooms, Fetch, and BoxRelay tasks, alongside the same extended-path and correlated-Gaussian scenarios. Section 4 and Appendix C retain identical coverage.

E2.justification: Experiment 1 and Tables 1–2 retain the same exhaustive path-enumeration baseline for VaR/CVaR estimation. No comparator is added, removed, or revised in any reported comparison.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, risk levels, bucket settings, empirical-quantile metrics, training budgets, and testing procedures in Section 4 and Appendix C are unchanged. The new sampling-cost discussion does not revise an experimental setting.

E4.justification: The sample-size and bucket sensitivity studies, agent-count scaling experiment, and correlated-loss robustness analysis are retained unchanged in Figures 3–4. Appendix case discussions also remain identical.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 95% Clopper-Pearson intervals for empirical quantiles in Figure 3 and Table 1. Repeated-run, seed, and uncertainty-estimation disclosures are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2–4 and Tables 1–2 retain identical results and findings. For example, Table 1 reports BoxRelay VaR estimates of 176 for BucketedVaR and 175 for the baseline at risk level 0.1 in both versions.

T1.justification: Definitions, equations, Theorems 1–2, and their Appendix B proofs are unchanged. The added qualitative sample-complexity limitation introduces no mathematical bound, assumption, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution list, and main conclusion retain the same claims about risk minimization, asymptotic near-optimality, and empirical effectiveness. The additions concern practical limitations and future work.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly acknowledges that accurate risk estimates can require many samples and distinguishes path identification from risk estimation. Section 6 explains that the previously suggested bandit approach could reduce sampling needs by bypassing risk-measure computation.

D1.justification: Section 7 and Appendix C retain the same policy-training details, hyperparameters, hardware disclosure, and statement that code and reproduction instructions accompany the supplementary materials.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 and the cited-work set are unchanged. Tan et al. (2022) and Ayyagari and Dukkipati (2021) already supported the bandit future direction in v3; v4 expands its practical motivation.

P1.justification: V4 adds short passages to Sections 5–6, an NSF funding acknowledgement, and an updated arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining wording, main section order, and appendix text are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added prose extends Section 5 onto page 10, and the acknowledgement shifts subsequent text and bibliography layout through page 13. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–2 retain their displays and captions.

improvement.justification: V4 modestly improves transparency by explicitly acknowledging the sampling cost of accurate risk estimation and explaining the motivation for optimizing paths without estimating risk measures. This clarifies a practical limitation omitted from v3's limitations section. The proposed bandit savings remain untested, while the method, proofs, and empirical evidence are unchanged.
